notes:
Synthetic sample document created by backend/scripts/create_phase14_sample_document.py. document_id is the document filename, which evaluate.py resolves to a real UUID through GET /documents.

Version 2 (Phase 15): expanded from 8 to 21 cases so retrieval claims rest on more than one example. Coverage by category:
- direct factual questions: case-001, case-003, case-004, case-005, case-009, case-010
- paraphrased questions: case-002, case-012, case-015
- terminology mismatch: case-016 (submitted vs filed), case-014 (pro-rated refund), case-018 (deductible repeated in Section 1 and Section 6)
- answer near a chunk boundary: case-013 (end of Section 2 sits at a chunk boundary under CHUNK_SIZE=500)
- repeated/common terms in multiple sections: case-017 (notice/days in Sections 4 and 5), case-018
- policy-specific terminology: case-009 (policy year), case-014 (pro-rated refund), case-011 (indemnification)
- unanswerable questions: case-006, case-007, case-019, case-020, case-021 (plus case-008, the pre-existing empty-query input case)
- semantically similar distractors: deliberately NOT scored as refusals. A cosine threshold is topical, so document-adjacent absent topics (dental coverage, maternity waiting period, coinsurance, prescription drugs) are retrieved on purpose; rejecting them at retrieval time would require semantic, not vector, judgement. They are exercised in scripts/test_phase15_retrieval_quality.py instead, where the assertion is that they still return only chunks owned by the queried document.
- specific-page questions: not covered. The sample document is a single page, so no multi-page fixture exists yet; recorded as a known limitation rather than silently skipped.

Every case was checked against the live API before being added. Cases were not added or removed to chase a target score.
